  "markdown_report": "At 0% progress, retain **recent-prefix top-10 auxiliary supervision** as a controlled hypothesis. Preserve the corrected NextItNet and its main loss; add weak recent-prefix boundary supervision. No new training or validation results are available.

**Insights from the supplied evidence.** (1) Users prefer specific recent connections over broadly related recommendations, motivating recent-prefix supervision without establishing intent labels. (2) Older isolated interests persist; cropping removes older evidence but may discard useful preferences. (3) Electronics has 12.27% sampled negative wins and a −0.2595 lower-tail margin, motivating discrimination improvements without establishing validation performance. (4) Embedding scores near 0.5 indicate near-zero mean cosine similarity, providing little evidence for collapse intervention.

**Literature insights.** Top-k calibration results warn that intuitive ranking surrogates need separate consistency proofs [Yang–Koyejo]. Top-K Pairwise Ranking and k-order statistic losses substantially limit novelty. CL4SRec motivates augmentation controls, while SSS4SR shows that changed target coverage can explain gains. Sampled-metric comparisons can differ from catalog comparisons [Krichene–Rendle]; matching 99 negatives supplies only partial alignment.

| Direction | Existing approach | Practical gap |
|---|---|---|
| Context selection | Suffix supervision; NextItNet | Ambiguous recent evidence; extra supervision confounds |
| Ranking objective | CE; SoftmaxLoss@K; top-k surrogates | Boundary instability; unproved calibration |
| Item specificity | Recformer-inspired text sharing | No compatibility or purpose labels |

Three candidates remain. Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment gives a positive (+) and negative (−).

- **Recent-prefix cutoff auxiliary: 3/6/7/7/5.** O: + diagnosis-specific combination; − established ingredients. P: + cheap deployment; − uncertain generalization. U: + targets stale interests and broad matches; − no intent labels. M: + boundary discrimination; − unstable sparse gradients. D: + small loss; − careful causal sampling and controls.
- **Full-prefix cutoff auxiliary: 2/6/4/7/3.** O: + focused adaptation; − close ranking precedents. P: + inexpensive isolation; − narrow contribution. U: + sharper competition; − no recency mechanism. M: + cutoff alignment; − unchanged context errors. D: + no cropping; − candidate-support integration.
- **Joint title-token mean encoder: 3/6/6/6/6.** O: + constrained text sharing; − established approach. P: + transferable lexical evidence; − uncertain sparse supervision. U: + item specificity; − overlap can reinforce broad matches. M: + shared item features; − no guaranteed separation. D: + simple pooling; − vocabulary, caching and export changes.

**Selected algorithm.** For at most one eligible target per batch row, encode its recent prefix and score the positive against 99 unique uniform negatives. Add 0.25·softplus(s₁₀⁻−s⁺), temperature 1, to the unchanged main loss. Without ties, dividing this loss by log 2 upper-bounds the sampled miss indicator; this is no calibration guarantee. Only the positive and boundary negative receive direct score gradients, which switch at boundary ties.

The idea explicitly targets stale-interest persistence, broad matches displacing specific recent matches, and weak sampled separation. Compare matched repeated-full-prefix CE, suffix CE, full-prefix boundary and suffix boundary controls as budget permits; preserve targets, candidates and loss reductions. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10. Deploy one complete-prefix checkpoint per category. Compatibility, duplication, satisfied needs and catalog improvement remain unestablished.",

    "description": "Add a weak recent-prefix top-10-boundary auxiliary loss to the corrected NextItNet’s unchanged full-prefix objective. Treat the intervention as a controlled combination of context cropping and sampled cutoff supervision, with direct precedents in augmentation and order-statistic ranking. Train one network per category and deploy only its complete-prefix forward pass.",
    "motivation": "The supplied user diagnosis identifies both older or isolated interests persisting despite coherent recent behavior and broadly related recommendations outranking specific recent matches. Recent-prefix auxiliary training removes older evidence for selected examples; cutoff supervision additionally emphasizes whether the observed target crosses a sampled tenth-place boundary. These mechanisms explicitly address two user-facing failures, but their effectiveness is hypothetical: observed next items provide no direct labels for current purpose, compatibility, duplication, mood or satisfied needs. Electronics’ supplied 12.27% negative-win rate and −0.2595 tenth-percentile margin motivate improved sampled discrimination, satisfying the model-facing alignment requirement without implying that these fitted-position diagnostics predict validation HR@10. At 0% progress, retain this small training-only hypothesis ahead of timestamp-dependent inference changes or a text pipeline. Evaluate the simpler full-prefix boundary alternative first when needed to isolate loss effects; a suffix variant is justified only if matched controls support its additional value.",
    "implementation_notes": "The corrected baseline source and its constructor, sampler, training entry point, and predictor writer are absent from the supplied text. Consequently, the code below is an executable PyTorch auxiliary-loss component under an explicit scoring contract, not a replacement train.py. Reconstructing the missing baseline would risk changing the supplied cold start and host interfaces. No tools, filesystem inspection, training, validation, or independent literature verification were performed. Literature descriptions rely on the supplied search material. A fully reproducible host integration still requires the concrete baseline source and settings.

Preserve the baseline NextItNet backbone, full-prefix objective, optimizer, batch size, sequence length, checkpoint-selection rule, and family-specific sample_batch. The experimental addition is loss = baseline_loss + 0.25 * auxiliary_loss, initially using temperature 1. Start from the corrected cold start, never a previous trial checkpoint. The coefficient is a prespecified starting hypothesis, not an established optimum. Keep the unnormalized softplus in optimization; dividing by log(2) is used only to state the pointwise bound. Normalizing the implemented loss would change the effective auxiliary weight.

Strengthen the comparison plan without automatically launching a large sweep. Retain the unchanged baseline as the zero-auxiliary reference. On identical selected targets and candidates, the informative control grid is input context {complete causal prefix, recent suffix} crossed with auxiliary objective {candidate CE, boundary softplus}. Every variant retains the same main loss. Complete-prefix CE supplies an extra-supervision/dropout control, suffix CE tests context change under CE, complete-prefix boundary tests cutoff supervision without cropping, and suffix boundary is the proposed combination. Run controls sequentially only within a predeclared remaining-budget allocation; if the grid cannot fit, report exactly which comparisons are missing and avoid attributing improvements to their unisolated mechanisms. The complete-prefix CE branch is not an exact duplicate of the main objective unless its targets, candidates, reduction, and scoring all coincide with that objective. A genuinely duplicated deterministic main loss merely rescales its gradient; independent dropout additionally changes stochastic supervision.

Match selected target positions, candidate IDs, auxiliary support, coefficient, temperature, optimizer updates, validation schedule, and loss reductions across the auxiliary controls. Use a common saved or deterministically generated training manifest wherever the baseline supports it. Keep the same dropout configuration and independent main/auxiliary dropout passes in all controls; matching seeds alone cannot guarantee identical masks when execution shapes or RNG consumption differ. Record those differences. Equal updates and equal GPU time generally cannot both be guaranteed, so report both realized compute and updates rather than claiming both are matched. If resources remain, a single smaller prespecified coefficient can test weight sensitivity; include zero through the baseline and avoid an open-ended weight sweep.

A length-matched random-context comparison is a lower-priority recency-specific control. Construct an input window entirely before the unchanged target and record its lag from the target. Random contiguous windows that end earlier than the recent suffix also alter target distance and omit intervening events; they are not clean evidence for recency alone. Never shift a target into its own context or relabel arbitrary cropped interiors as immediately preceding that target. No augmentation control establishes that cropping preserves sufficient semantic evidence. CL4SRec studies contrastive views and augmentation-only controls, not a verified NextItNet supervised-suffix advantage. SSS4SR directly motivates holding target coverage and frequency fixed because additional supervision can explain apparent gains.

Compute the actual maximum receptive-field span from every stride-one temporal convolution on the deepest causal path: R = 1 + sum((kernel_size - 1) * dilation). Count the actual convolutions rather than assuming a generic block topology. Choose suffix length 8 when R > 8, otherwise max(1, R - 1); reject this context intervention if R <= 1. Verify that sequence-wide normalization, pooling, position-dependent features, or other dependencies do not invalidate the local calculation or repacking equivalence. Measure the fraction of selected positions where cropping removes accessible evidence. A crop retaining the entire receptive field can be deterministically equivalent to the full prefix under matching padding, position and normalization semantics; dropout differences alone do not demonstrate historical exclusion.

For each batch row, uniformly select one valid prediction position having more than suffix_length visible nonpadding inputs. Use exactly those eligible positions in complete-prefix and suffix controls. This bounds auxiliary encoding to at most B sequences and prevents the full-prefix controls from receiving additional short-history targets. The supplied positive at position t must occur strictly after the input prefix ending at t. Copy only input positions at or before t. For the suffix branch retain their last suffix_length nonpadding IDs, and left-pad to the baseline length. For the complete-prefix branch retain the available causal prefix. Never insert the prediction target into its own input. Count short-history rows, invalid positions, catalog-support failures, selected examples, and effective auxiliary contributions separately. Selecting only long-enough prefixes changes the auxiliary training population and can underrepresent sparse histories.

For every selected position, the integration must provide [positive, 99 negatives]. Draw negatives uniformly without replacement from mapped nonpadding training-catalog IDs, excluding the target and causally observed prefix positives. Do not use later training events, validation labels or test labels for exclusions. Preserve the actual sampler’s user/prefix mapping, including truncated-away earlier history only where already available causally. Use complete-prefix exclusions for both crop controls so the candidate population is identical. This auxiliary policy must be documented if the baseline main loss uses another support. Require at least 99 eligible negatives; skip and count unsupported rows instead of repeating IDs or silently changing the boundary. Sampling without replacement must be genuine, not bounded rejection followed by duplicate filling. Unobserved candidates can be false negatives; prefix exclusion reduces some contradictory supervision but does not identify all relevant alternatives and may suppress repeat-consumption competitors.

The loss uses the tenth-highest score among 99 negatives, with gradients through that selected score and the positive. Without ties, sampled HR@10 equals 1{s_positive > s_negative_10}. For z = (s_negative_10 - s_positive)/temperature with positive temperature, softplus(z)/log(2) is at least one on strict misses and therefore pointwise upper-bounds the miss indicator. This algebraic bound gives neither population calibration nor consistency for the restricted NextItNet model or the actual sampled training distribution. Yang–Koyejo’s calibration analysis and Top-K Pairwise Ranking’s results apply to their specified objectives and assumptions; they do not prove this single-boundary surrogate consistent. Unrestricted CE consistency also does not imply consistency under this architecture, sampling design, or mixed objective.

Away from score ties, the direct score derivatives are sigmoid(z)/temperature for the selected boundary negative and its negative for the positive, before averaging. Other negatives receive zero direct score derivative through this auxiliary loss, including negatives ranked above the boundary. Shared network parameters still couple item and sequence representations. The loss is continuous and piecewise differentiable, with boundary-identity switches redirecting the negative gradient. At temperature 1 this remains a structural instability risk. Smaller temperatures can strengthen miss gradients and saturate comfortable hits; do not launch a temperature sweep initially. Do not detach the boundary. Record finite losses and gradients, boundary-score gaps, selected-boundary item coverage, and boundary-identity changes on a small fixed permitted diagnostic sample when affordable. These measurements assess optimization behavior, not validation success. Tie ranking follows the host evaluator, while topk gradient allocation at equal scores is implementation-dependent; do not claim exact tie-aware objective equivalence.

No proposal-probability correction is applied: this is a deliberately sampled ranking surrogate, not an unbiased catalog objective. Matching 99 negatives and candidate uniqueness supplies only partial alignment. Eligibility rules, item sampling, user weighting, target positions and loss all matter. The training exclusion policy is not asserted to reproduce the pinned evaluator’s policy. Do not change the evaluator to make that claim true. With one positive, sampled HR@10 equals sampled Recall@10, but neither equals full-catalog HR@10. For M eligible catalog negatives and R strict outrankers, uniform sampling without replacement succeeds when a hypergeometric draw of 99 contains at most nine outrankers, whereas catalog success requires R <= 9. This illustration assumes the stated uniform support and ignores ties; it is not a claim about undocumented host eligibility details.

Make weighting explicit. Averaging one selected auxiliary example per eligible batch row gives equal weight to supported rows in that batch, not necessarily to distinct users across training. Uniform interaction sampling favors active users; uniform user sampling followed by a global token-average main loss can still favor long histories. Preserve and document the baseline user sampler and main-loss reduction rather than silently replacing them. Report the auxiliary/main weighting mismatch and long-history eligibility bias. Separate category models and macro validation selection do not imply that unequal per-category training compute or target counts have been normalized. All-position historical supervision also differs from evaluation on one final held-out target per user. Negative-count matching does not remove this context mismatch.

Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum epochs 200, and 200 batches per completed epoch. Use dedicated auxiliary position/candidate RNG streams seeded 42, separate from the baseline sampler and diagnostic RNGs; record their actual libraries and states. Preserve all four datasets and routing. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Use one GPU per trial and charge training, auxiliary encoding, diagnostics, failures and export checks to the shared 43,200 GPU-second allowance. Four concurrent slots do not multiply it. Record actual updates, processed main/auxiliary positions, eligible/skipped crop counts, effective coefficient, GPU seconds, parameters, peak memory, and every validation query. Additional auxiliary computation prevents simultaneous assumptions of equal updates and equal compute.

Select only through unchanged host macro validation HR@10: 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negatives, evaluation seed 42. Preserve the baseline validation/checkpoint schedule and report all four category outcomes alongside the macro score when supplied. Do not invent local benchmark substitutes or access hidden tests. One additional validation hit changes macro HR by 0.00125. Repeated adaptive comparisons can overfit this finite sample; predeclare comparison order and any conditional extra controls, log all queries, and freeze configuration before the separate final evaluation. Additional candidate samples or full-catalog validation may be reported only if the unchanged host already supports them; they are not substitutes for selection and additional samples do not establish catalog equivalence. Keep claims restricted to sampled-candidate validation gains unless separate permitted evidence exists. Supplied inspiration scores are contextual observations, not paired evidence for this proposal; the −1 result does not identify a failure cause.

The intervention may exploit training-item popularity, frequent lexical patterns already encoded through IDs, target repetition, or high-activity users rather than specific recent intent. Repeated sampled targets can amplify memorization, and the boundary can focus on ambiguous positives or noisy candidates. Track target frequency, candidate coverage and training-frequency distributions as risk indicators using permitted training data; these are not relevance labels. Stronger fitted margins, lower auxiliary loss or a better pointwise bound do not prove improved held-out ranking. Embedding scores near 0.5 still do not justify a collapse intervention. A failed boundary comparison should leave full-prefix CE or the unchanged baseline as legitimate separately trained alternatives, never trigger score fusion.

Preserve ModelView.model as the actual trained nn.Module and retain item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data. Keep DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), its metrics and metric_definitions outputs, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). The diagnostic loader continues yielding (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors. Auxiliary candidates remain internal to training. Measure standard diagnostic margins on supplied negatives and deployed complete-prefix features. Label new candidate-boundary statistics separately with their support, temperature, candidate policy and definitions; they are not validation HR. Stable user identities cannot be inferred from anonymous loader rows. Item-category breakdowns remain unavailable because item categories are not provided; do not fabricate them from routing categories or interpret empty breakdowns as measured absence of failures.

Continue the native twenty-user full-catalog unseen-item diagnosis, five real training users/category. Track stale-interest rejection, broad-match rejection, preference for lower-ranked specific items and uncertain item identity separately when native outputs support them. Track duplication and compatibility rejections as unresolved outcomes rather than expected successes. Do not derive quantitative rejection rates from qualitative summaries. This proposal needs no metadata. Only permitted histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions may be used; ratings, reviews, prices, stores, item categories, pretrained weights and simulator traits remain unavailable despite generic example schemas.

Inference architecture is unchanged. Preserve padding-safe causal convolutions, zero padding states and positionwise normalization. Read the final nonpadding position by positional maximum, never count minus one, and retain the corrected baseline’s explicit empty-history policy. Preserve the embedded predictor writer’s architecture, configuration, mappings and checkpoint keys. Each category loads exactly one independently trained checkpoint; there is no auxiliary inference pass, checkpoint averaging, score fusion, separately fitted component or independent expert. Verify generated-predictor reload score agreement on identical permitted inputs and all four routes. In-memory view/network agreement alone does not establish export parity. Check causal target alignment, finite auxiliary gradients, unique candidates, padding correctness, empty-history handling and the full-prefix/suffix control manifest with small bounded checks charged to the search budget.

For reproducibility, the host integration must additionally record concrete architecture and receptive field, optimizer and schedule, batch size, sequence length, precision, gradient clipping, regularization, sampler support, target-position manifest, validation cadence, checkpoint rule, library versions and GPU model. Preserve inherited settings unless explicitly varied. The supplied component assumes predict_score accepts N x D features and N x 100 candidate IDs; if the baseline uses another signature, implement and verify a thin adapter to its actual scoring head rather than replacing that head with an assumed dot product. Missing baseline integration and unexecuted controls remain explicit limitations; no completed results are claimed.",
    "pseudocode": "import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


def recent_prefix_auxiliary(model, sequence, positive, candidate_ids,
                            selected_positions, suffix_length,
                            temperature=1.0, control='boundary',
                            context='suffix'):
    """Executable auxiliary component under the declared scoring contract.

    Host retains its supplied corrected NextItNet train.py.
    sequence, positive: B x L baseline-aligned tensors.
    selected_positions: B vector; -1 skips a row.
    candidate_ids: B x 100, [target, 99 unique negatives] on selected rows.
    Host samples candidates from declared causal training support.
    model.log2feats: N x L -> N x L x D.
    model.predict_score: N x D, N x 100 -> N x 100.
    Use the same positions/candidates/support across context/loss controls.
    """
    if temperature <= 0 or suffix_length < 1:
        raise ValueError('Invalid temperature or suffix length')
    if control not in ('boundary', 'ce'):
        raise ValueError('Unknown auxiliary objective')
    if context not in ('full', 'suffix'):
        raise ValueError('Unknown context control')
    if sequence.ndim != 2 or positive.shape != sequence.shape:
        raise ValueError('Expected aligned B x L sequence and positive tensors')
    batch_size, length = sequence.shape
    if selected_positions.shape != (batch_size,):
        raise ValueError('Expected one selected position per batch row')
    if candidate_ids.shape != (batch_size, 100):
        raise ValueError('Expected positive plus 99 negative candidate IDs')

    rows, crops = [], []
    for row in range(batch_size):
        t = int(selected_positions[row].item())
        if t < 0:
            continue
        if t >= length or sequence[row, t] == 0 or positive[row, t] == 0:
            raise ValueError('Selected position must be a valid input/target pair')
        prefix = sequence[row, :t + 1]
        visible = prefix[prefix.ne(0)]
        # Identical long-prefix eligibility in BOTH context controls.
        if visible.numel() <= suffix_length:
            continue
        ids = candidate_ids[row]
        if ids[0] != positive[row, t]:
            raise ValueError('Candidate zero must equal the aligned next target')
        if torch.any(ids <= 0) or torch.unique(ids).numel() != 100:
            raise ValueError('Candidates must be nonpadding and unique')
        if torch.isin(ids[1:], visible).any():
            raise ValueError('Negative overlaps the visible causal prefix')
        # Host also checks available truncated-away causal exclusions.
        # Repacking assumes corrected baseline position/padding semantics.
        retained = visible[-suffix_length:] if context == 'suffix' else visible
        crop = torch.zeros_like(sequence[row])
        crop[-retained.numel():] = retained
        rows.append(row)
        crops.append(crop)

    if not rows:
        return model.item_emb.weight.sum() * 0.0, 0

    row_ids = torch.tensor(rows, device=sequence.device, dtype=torch.long)
    cropped_sequence = torch.stack(crops)
    features = model.log2feats(cropped_sequence)
    positions = torch.arange(length, device=sequence.device)[None, :]
    last = torch.where(cropped_sequence.ne(0), positions, -1).amax(dim=1)
    if torch.any(last < 0):
        raise ValueError('Auxiliary contexts must be nonempty')
    h = features[torch.arange(len(rows), device=sequence.device), last]
    scores = model.predict_score(h, candidate_ids[row_ids])
    if scores.shape != (len(rows), 100):
        raise ValueError('Scoring adapter must return one score per candidate')
    scores = scores.float()
    if not torch.isfinite(scores).all():
        raise FloatingPointError('Nonfinite auxiliary scores')

    if control == 'ce':
        labels = torch.zeros(len(rows), device=scores.device, dtype=torch.long)
        loss = F.cross_entropy(scores / temperature, labels)
    else:
        tenth_negative = scores[:, 1:].topk(10, dim=1).values[:, -1]
        # Keep the selected boundary attached to autograd.
        # No /log(2) normalization in optimization: coefficient stays 0.25.
        loss = F.softplus(
            (tenth_negative - scores[:, 0]) / temperature
        ).mean()
    if not torch.isfinite(loss):
        raise FloatingPointError('Nonfinite auxiliary loss')
    return loss, len(rows)

# HOST INTEGRATION; baseline-specific APIs are not invented:
# 1. Preserve corrected NextItNet, sample_batch and aligned main objective.
# 2. Determine actual causal receptive field and suffix length as specified.
# 3. Using dedicated RNG streams(seed=42), uniformly select one eligible
#    causal target position per row, or -1; record skipped/support counts.
# 4. Uniformly sample 99 distinct negatives without replacement from declared
#    causal eligible support. Never inspect future/held-out interactions.
#    Skip/count rows with fewer than 99 eligible negatives.
# 5. Reuse target/candidate manifests across independently trained controls:
#      unchanged baseline (weight=0)
#      full-prefix auxiliary CE
#      suffix auxiliary CE
#      full-prefix auxiliary boundary
#      suffix auxiliary boundary
#    Allocate controls before execution; do not assume all fit the budget.
# 6. auxiliary_loss, support = recent_prefix_auxiliary(...)
#    loss = unchanged_baseline_loss + 0.25 * auxiliary_loss
#    Average auxiliary loss once over supported selected rows.
# 7. Keep baseline optimizer, validation cadence and checkpoint-selection rule.
#    Record main-loss reduction, row/user sampling and target-frequency bias.
# 8. Verify finite gradients, target alignment, candidate uniqueness,
#    padding/causality, all category routes and generated-predictor reload.
# 9. Export one selected independently trained checkpoint per category.
#    Never combine control predictions or checkpoints.
#
# All epochs <=200; 200 batches/completed epoch; preprocessing seed=0;
# training seed=42; single-GPU; all four routes retained;
# DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; artifacts beneath trial directory.
# Charge training/diagnostics/failures/checks to 43,200 shared GPU-seconds.
# Deploy complete-prefix features with positional-maximum nonpadding readout
# and the corrected baseline's explicit empty-history policy.
# Keep DiagnosisProbe, ModelView and interpreter contracts unchanged.
# Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10; no new results are claimed.",

    }
